skill1: Only when at 100%: Dodging Bullets: Invulnerable for 2 sec.

caveats: ⚑ Extrasensory is modeled as a resource pool (initial 100, max 100) decaying 1 point per 2 sec (= 0.5%/s) and re-filled to 100 by her own burst. The three continuous tier buffs are re-evaluated on a 2-sec interval with durationSec 2 (self-refreshing) instead of as true always-on passives, because a `passive` trigger's resourceGate would be evaluated ONCE at frame 0 and could never lapse. Consequences: (a) the tiers are COLD for the first 2 sec of the fight (interval first-fires at t=sec, not t=0) — ~1.1% of a 180 s fight; (b) a threshold crossing is honored with up to 2 sec of latency.

⚑ Threshold arithmetic: kit says 'above 70/55/25%' (strict). Decay is integer points, so strict-above == resourceGate min 71/56/26. Blocks are ordered gates-then-decay so each tick reads the PRE-decay pool, matching kit reading order.

⚑ 'Normal attacks deal true damage for 10 sec' has NO non-weaponSwap channel in the schema — `trueNormals` exists only on weaponSwap. It is modeled as a mirror-swap (same class SMG, same ammo 120, damagePct = her datamined normalAttackMultiplier 10.12, base cadence inherited) whose ONLY intended effect is the true flavor. If the engine grants a fresh magazine or alters cadence on swap entry, this block adds damage the kit does not — verify shot-count parity before trusting it (recipe in flags).
⚑ The 48-hit 472.18% rider is true-flavored, so it is amplified by her own True Damage ▲ 48.62% (S1) — the two lines interact; a mis-scoped trueDamagePct would double-count into this rider.
Hit Rate ▲ 22.37% is carried as hitRatePct (the ⚑ HR→core lift path, sim.ts hrCoreMult). The kit percentage is literal; the core-rate CONVERSION is unmeasured for this unit.

Invulnerability (100% tier) is unmodeled: the v1 boss deals no damage and no roster consumer reads a 'Dodging Bullets' status. It costs zero damage but IS a real kit line — re-check if a defensive/HP model or a status consumer ever lands.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Chisato (SMG/Iron/Attacker/B3) is a self-contained self-buff attacker built on the Extrasensory gauge: S1 fills it to 100% at battle start, it decays 1 point per 2 sec (0.5%/s), and her burst re-fills it to 100%. Three nested charge tiers (>70% ATK ▲53.69%, >55% True Damage ▲48.62%, >25% Hit Rate ▲22.37%) are modeled as interval-2s resourceGated self-buffs (durationSec 2, self-refreshing) so they can genuinely LAPSE as the gauge drains — a passive would latch at frame 0 forever. Derived trajectory from a refill: >70 tier drops at t≈60 s, >55 at t≈90 s, >25 at t≈150 s; in a comp where she bursts every rotation (~20 s) the pool stays in [80,100] and all three tiers hold all fight. S2 gives a 10 s true-damage window on her own burst cast (modeled via a mirror weaponSwap with trueNormals — the only schema channel; ⚑ ammo/cadence parity unverified) plus a per-48-normal-hit 472.18% true-damage rider (crit-eligible per RIDERCRIT, no core — the text does not say core strike, FB by timing left ON). Burst re-fills Extrasensory and grants ATK ▲73.16% for 10 s. Only the 100%-tier invulnerability is unmodeled.

flags.field: base cadence (pullsPerSec / reloadFrames 81) — affects every block
flags.estimate: SMG effective ~20 pulls/s (nominal rate snapped to 60fps frame boundaries: 60/ceil(60/nominal)); reload ≈ 81f = 1.35 s
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #1: datamined rate_of_fire / reloadFrames are known-unreliable and a datamined rate is NOMINAL. Cadence sets both her shot count and the 48-hit rider's period (~2.4 s/proc at 20/s, ignoring reload gaps) — it is the single largest lever on this unit's total.
flags.recipe: Read the ammo counter frame-by-frame on a chisato solo recording (rounds spent per second = shots/s, the directly-measured quantity); confirm the magazine drain time for 120 rounds and the reload gap. Do NOT infer cadence from burst-gauge/FB counts (downstream of gauge-per-shot).

flags.estimate: Mirror-swap: damagePct 10.12, weapon SMG, maxAmmo 120, base cadence inherited, durationSec 10 — intended to be damage-neutral EXCEPT the true flavor
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #3 (weapon-swap shot economy is kit-silent). Chisato has NO weapon swap in her kit; `trueNormals` only exists on weaponSwap, so the flavor flip is expressed through a channel that may carry side effects (a fresh magazine on swap entry, a forced reload on swap exit, a different core/range path). Cannot be settled from prose. Under-modeling instead would drop a real 10s×N-rotations true-damage window that is itself amplified by her own True Damage ▲48.62%, so the block ships flagged rather than skipped (HARD RULE: never auto-skip weapon-state lines).
flags.recipe: In-memory A/B with withPatchedOverride('chisato', …): run controlComp('chisato') with the swap block present vs removed and count `shot` events + `reload` events for chisato. If shot count differs by more than rounding, the swap is perturbing the ammo economy — replace it with a no-op-economy variant (drop maxAmmo, or move the line to unmodeled with the true-damage loss documented). Then confirm against footage that her burst-window popups are white/true-flavored and un-DEF-reduced.

flags.estimate: 22.37 Hit-Rate points → core-rate lift via the engine's hrCoreMult path; magnitude of the resulting core-rate change unknown for an SMG at scope-lock range
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #7: the kit PERCENTAGE is literal, but the Hit-Rate→core conversion is measured-only. On an SMG with coreAttackMultiplier 250 the core share is a large fraction of her total, so the conversion slope, not the kit number, decides her damage.
flags.recipe: Cross-check against the accuracy-circle geometry set (docs/data/sg-calc/, HRCORE) for an SMG at the scope-lock band; if a chisato recording exists, count CORE HIT popups per magazine with and without the tier live (gauge above vs below 25%) and fit the core rate.

flags.estimate: DERIVED from kit-stated start + decay + refill: 100 at t=0, −0.5 points/s; from any refill the >70 tier lapses at t≈60 s, >55 at t≈90 s, >25 at t≈150 s. In a B1+B2+chisato rotation (own burst ≈ every 20 s) the pool holds in [80,100] and all three tiers stay live for the whole fight; the >70% ATK tier is the first to be at risk.
flags.reasoning: Prior 10 says DERIVE when start + consume + rebuild are kit-stated — they are (fill 100 / −1 per 2 s / burst refill), so the trajectory is arithmetic, not a guess. What is NOT kit-derivable is her own burst CADENCE, which is comp-dependent; that is what makes tier uptime a ⚑ rather than a fact.
flags.recipe: Instrument via cfg.onEvent: log burstCast frames for chisato in the graded comp and compute max inter-burst gap; if any gap exceeds 60 s the ATK tier genuinely lapses and the interval-gate encoding is load-bearing. Cross-check against footage: the ATK/True-Damage tier drop should be visible as a step down in popup magnitude ~60 s after her last burst.

flags.field: override.skill1[0..2] (interval:2 + durationSec:2 re-evaluation of continuous buffs)
flags.estimate: Tiers cold for t∈[0,2) s (interval first-fires at t=sec per the engine convention), and threshold crossings honored with ≤2 s latency
flags.reasoning: The kit calls these buffs 'continuous', but a `passive` trigger evaluates its resourceGate once at frame 0 and could never lapse as the gauge drains — that would over-credit any fight where the gauge falls below a tier. The 2-sec re-evaluation is the faithful-direction approximation; its cost is a ~1.1% cold opening on a 180 s fight (a small UNDER-credit).
flags.recipe: Read buffApply events for stat atkPct/trueDamagePct/hitRatePct on chisato: confirm the first apply is at frame 120 and that applies repeat every 120 frames with no gap (refresh:true), and that they STOP within one tick of the gauge crossing 70/55/25. If the engine honors durationSec on a `passive`, replace tier blocks 1–3 with a passive opener + the interval refresher to close the t=0–2 s hole.

flags.estimate: 48 LANDED normal-attack hits ⇒ 48 rounds at hitsPerShot 1; ~2.4 s of fire at 20/s, so roughly one proc per 2.5–3 s including reload gaps
flags.reasoning: The kit says 'landing 48 normal attack(s)' — the engine's hitCount counts ROUNDS, not pulls, and does not model whiffs. Whole-picture check: 120 ammo / 48 = 2.5 procs per magazine, which is consistent and non-absurd; but if the engine counts rounds FIRED where the game counts rounds LANDED, procs come slightly early.
flags.recipe: Count the 472.18% true-damage popups per magazine on a chisato recording — expect 2–3 per full 120-round belt. If observed procs are fewer, the game is gating on landed hits and an accuracy haircut belongs on the threshold.
